title: I've been building a sci-fi courier RPG where you can leave your apartment, drive through the city, then fly straight into orbit with GPT 5.6 Sol and then later on Astra.
author: JayB_Official
selftext:
kept this project mostly to myself while I've been building it, but it's finally getting to the point where I feel comfortable showing actual uninterrupted gameplay.

This is AUTOMATON: THE LOST COURIER.

You play a courier living in NIGHTLINE, a massive city built across the surface of NIGHTWORLD. The idea is that the world isn't separated into a bunch of disconnected levels.

In this footage I start in the character creator, wake up in my apartment, walk downstairs into the city, get into my vehicle, fly up through the towers, leave the surface, reach the orbital megastructure, land on it, get back out, and walk around.

It's all part of the same playable world.

The scale of the game has honestly gotten a little ridiculous. 😭

The long-term goal is less "save the universe" and more live a life inside a gigantic strange place. Deliveries, jobs, vehicles, NPCs with persistent lives and memories, apartments, businesses, exploration, crime, transit, the orbital settlements, and eventually the neighboring world of NEMORA.

The story is there, but I don't want the player to feel like the universe stops existing whenever they're not doing the main quest.

Also, full transparency: this is an extremely AI-assisted project. I'm not pretending otherwise. I've been directing it, testing it, rejecting things, redesigning systems, breaking it, fixing it, and iterating on it continuously across a frankly stupid number of builds. 😂 It's been much closer to an ongoing development process than a one-prompt game generation.

This is still early gameplay alpha, so there are plenty of rough edges, unfinished systems, performance work, animations, and general weirdness left to solve.

But seeing the whole journey actually work now, from a tiny apartment room all the way out into orbit, is kinda fucking surreal.
